whatChangedSinceCP1: CP1 pre-registered the tri-state reading, the shared ArcGIS reader, the registry and the reactivation blast-radius guard. All four are as-built and committed; no design decision was reversed.

CP1 expected a single new test file (review-retired-parcel-nodes.test.mjs). As-built there are three test files plus the edited contract test, because the three concerns (the ArcGIS reader, the registry, the blast-radius refusal) are separable and each is asserted where it lives: county-parcel-id-currency.test.mjs, county-live-currency-sources.test.mjs, retired-reactivation-guard.test.mjs.

TWO DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY RUNNING THE CLI, not by writing it, and both are fixed in the PR: the request counter was read off the Map the Bastrop source returns (so the four ArcGIS counties would have reported a cost of 0 for a run that did make calls), and a whole-source transport failure reported the bare string 'fetch failed' with no cause. Measured after the fix, one county and one command with the TLS flag the only difference: source=unreachable/absent=0/unmeasured=1013 versus source=registered/absent=1013/unmeasured=0/requests=7.

CP1 named the registry entry for Caldwell as 'Prop_ID on Peter's Colony-style sibling service'; as-built it is Caldwell_County_Parcel_Map FeatureServer/1, layer name 'Parcels', field Prop_ID (esriFieldTypeInteger).

CP1 listed a fourth falsifier candidate ('every registered source exposes .requests'); it was promoted to a real test in county-live-currency-sources.test.mjs after defect 1 above proved the contract was not enforced anywhere.

theReaderItselfTwoFactsDiscoveredByAskin.dialect: the literal form is NOT uniform across the five services, so it is discovered rather than assumed. Travis PROP_ID (Integer) answers ArcGIS error 400 for PROP_ID IN ('1000025') and 200 for the bare form; Hays prop_id (also Integer) accepts the quoted form; Williamson QuickRefID (String) requires it. The reader tries the field-type-driven form first and retries the other form on an ArcGIS 400 before calling any id unmeasured.
theReaderItselfTwoFactsDiscoveredByAskin.cost: ids are batched 100 per IN (...), no geometry is requested, and the request count is reported by the run rather than assumed: 7 requests for Bastrop's 1,013 candidates, 2 for each ArcGIS namespace probe.

theReadersOwnLimitsStatedRatherThanDisco.idFieldIsAHandDeclaration: a field that answers 1 for every sampled real node id and 0 for the control is the node-id namespace; a field in a DIFFERENT namespace can also answer 1 for some ids by bare-number collision, and no probe can rule that out. The registration is therefore only as good as the sampled ids, and each entry names the ids it was verified against.
theReadersOwnLimitsStatedRatherThanDisco.bastropNeedsAUsablePolygon: the Bastrop entry reads 'absent' when BCAD has no ring for the prop_id, which includes records the county still publishes as POINTS. A point record is not an absence from the county's records -- it is the absence of a cadastral polygon. This is stated in the CLOSE's classification, where it accounts for 2 of the 1,013.
theReadersOwnLimitsStatedRatherThanDisco.theReviewReadsTheAtomsStoreOnly: the CLI's subject is parcel-node atoms with status='retired'. It has no visibility of the serving snapshot's retirement marks, which is the population OPS-16's four 'candidates' actually live in. Closing that is a different row, not a change to this one made quietly.
